q7.answer: Clients never copy the key. Each provider call (for example charge) asks the one process-wide secrets provider for get(name), which returns the current Secret from the immutable snapshot, and uses reveal() on it for that request. The refresher thread (or a forced re-read after a 401/403) swaps in a new snapshot atomically, so the next call sees the new key. A request already in flight keeps the value it read.

q8.answer: A three-part gate before revocation. (1) Every pod, job and script runs the new image digest, since only old-image pods hold old keys. (2) For every live pod in the cluster pod list, the latest secrets_refreshed log line shows the expected version ids (the latest in the store, matching the ticket) and is no older than one refresh interval plus a margin. (3) Each provider shows the old key's last-used time older than one refresh interval plus a margin that exceeds the provider's lag, with no unknown callers. Revoke nothing until all three pass.

q9.answer: Order: (1) inventory callers and check providers; (2) create store layout, KMS keys and access policies, proven with a probe secret; (3) issue new keys at the providers with old keys still active; (4) write the new keys into the store; (5) build, review and merge the code change that reads from the store and removes the keys from config/app.yaml (not merged before step 4), with staging drills first; (6) prod rolling deploy; (7) confirmation gate, then block rollback to old images, then revoke old keys at the providers. So: access, copy keys in, switch app, remove from file (in the same PR as the switch), and rotation spans the whole thing, with revocation last.

q10.answer: A local run (make run) defaults APP_ENV to dev and reads orders-api/dev/* from the secret store using the engineer's own login. Those paths hold provider sandbox keys, so live keys are never used locally. Engineers have no prod access, and the loader refuses APP_ENV=prod outside the prod identity. make run-offline uses an in-process fake backend with placeholder values and local stubs.

q11.answer: I never separately decided the case of a secret missing while the store is reachable. The document treats any failed fetch the same way, so the missing secret would be retried 3 times, 2 seconds apart (only the missing one), and then the pod logs an error naming the secret and exits non-zero without becoming ready, since all three keys are required. I did not distinguish a missing secret from an unreachable store or say it should fail faster.
